title: Write a blinker in Structured Text
summary: Build a blinker from a TON timer and a memory variable, and make it run only while an enable input is on.
scope: Tests provide native POSIX host evidence with one 10 ms task; they are not evidence of a physical lamp, hardware timing, HIL, or certification.
objectives: Write the timer-and-memory pattern that makes an output change state at a fixed interval.
Gate an output with an input so that it stops at once when the input drops.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/EnabledBlink.st, write the logic that makes Lamp change state every {{t:300}} ms while Enable is ON. The timer Clock and the memory LampOn are already declared. When Enable is OFF, Lamp must be OFF.
stages.checkpoint: You can describe the pattern: run a timer, toggle the memory when it expires, restart the timer.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Enable turns ON at {{t:100}} ms and OFF at {{t:1150}} ms. Predict Lamp at {{t:350}}, {{t:550}}, {{t:850}}, and {{t:1250}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:EnabledBlink.Lamp=false@350|OFF}} at {{t:350}} ms, {{v:EnabledBlink.Lamp=true@550|ON}} at {{t:550}} ms, {{v:EnabledBlink.Lamp=false@850|OFF}} at {{t:850}} ms, {{v:EnabledBlink.Lamp=false@1250|OFF}} at {{t:1250}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this flaw of the starting program, save it, then press Check: The starting program keeps Lamp OFF all the time, so it never turns ON at {{t:550}} ms. Run Clock with Enable and a preset of T#300ms. When Clock.Q is TRUE, invert LampOn and restart Clock. Set Lamp from LampOn and Enable, then save the file.
stages.checkpoint: Lamp follows LampOn only while Enable is ON.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named EnabledBlink and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow Lamp in the trace: it stays OFF until about {{t:400}} ms, which is {{t:300}} ms after Enable came ON, is ON until about {{t:700}} ms, ON again from about {{t:1000}} ms, and goes OFF at once at {{t:1150}} ms when Enable drops.
stages.checkpoint: The first ON starts about {{t:300}} ms after Enable came ON, not {{t:300}} ms after the program started.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A blinker that ignores Enable would already be ON at {{t:350}} ms. Which of your lines makes the difference?
stages.checkpoint: Starting the timer from Enable moves the first change, and the AND with Enable stops the lamp at once.

hints.text: The timer must only run while Enable is ON, so Enable is the IN of Clock.
Write Clock(IN := Enable, PT := T#300ms); IF Clock.Q THEN LampOn := NOT LampOn; Clock(IN := FALSE, PT := T#300ms); END_IF; Lamp := LampOn AND Enable;

faultCases: The starting program keeps Lamp OFF all the time, so it never turns ON at {{t:550}} ms.
